title: The public snapshot ships usage-rules.md, .intent_critic.yml and .prettierignore, which hv ruled stay in the workroom, and the exit-code contract lives in usage-rules.md (ST0010 Q1)
body:
hv ruled on 2026-10-27 (vc decision 78, ST0010's Q1, as vc recommended) on what the public snapshot ships beyond decision 52's allow-list:
- It ships VERSION, .gitignore, .gitattributes and design/.
- It leaves out usage-rules.md, a contract for working in this repository that points at AGENTS.md, which does not ship.
- It leaves out .intent_critic.yml and .prettierignore, which configure workroom tools. The critic's defaults equal that config.
tests/shipped.paths lists all seven. usage-rules.md is also load-bearing in shipped files, so dropping it from the list is not enough on its own.

## Measured

On main at 4ccfde65, git grep over the shipped list:
- **The exit-code contract.** usage-rules.md is the one place it is stated ("honour the exit codes", usage-rules.md:58). tests/unit/documentation.bats reads it there: `contract_exit_codes` (294-300), and the arms at 783-786 and 859. In a tree without usage-rules.md, those arms read nothing.
- **Comments citing usage-rules.md:** lib/builtins:306, lib/cmd/shell-init:6, tests/unit/buildfmt.bats:1011 and tests/unit/neutral.bats:27.
- **.prettierignore.** tests/unit/workroom.bats exempts it, beside .gitignore, from its pointer arm (25, 200). README.md:227 and docs/migration.md:39 tell users to fence the vendored runtime in their own project's .prettierignore. That is product advice and stays.
- **.intent_critic.yml** is named only by itself and by the list.
- **The release notes** (CHANGELOG.md, RELEASES/0.1.2.md and 0.1.11.md) mention usage-rules.md as history.

## Fix

- Drop the three files from tests/shipped.paths.
- Move the exit-code contract into a shipped document, the one place it is stated, and point documentation.bats's readers at it. usage-rules.md then points at that document rather than restating the list (Highlander).
- Reword the shipped comments that cite usage-rules.md so that they point at what ships.
- Drop workroom.bats's .prettierignore exemption.
- The release notes keep their history.

## Done when

1. tests/shipped.paths lists none of usage-rules.md, .intent_critic.yml or .prettierignore, and still lists VERSION, .gitignore, .gitattributes and design/.
2. The exit-code contract is stated once, in a shipped document. documentation.bats reads it there, and usage-rules.md points at it.
3. No shipped file other than the release notes names usage-rules.md or .intent_critic.yml. workroom.bats exempts no path that no longer ships.
4. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU (documentation.bats and workroom.bats, with the tree scans and help), and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

Fixed at c1e541abfad27eac4c33413b1751aef2b6942556, landed on main by vc with the rest of C (fb66b479..7565e2a2) on hv's GO of 29 Oct, as cc banked it. tests/shipped.paths no longer lists usage-rules.md, .intent_critic.yml or .prettierignore, and still lists VERSION, .gitignore, .gitattributes and design/ (hv's Q1, vc decision 78).

- **The contract's one statement** is the table under "Exit codes are a contract" in docs/authoring-commands.md, which ships. That table listed 0 to 5, so it had already gone stale beside usage-rules.md's line, which also listed 6. It gains 6 (devbin's own trees only: `use` refused in a project that vendors devbin) and says it is the one place the codes are listed. usage-rules.md now points at the table and lists nothing, and intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md names the table as the contract's home.
- **documentation.bats reads it there:** `contract_table` takes the rows under that heading, and `contract_exit_codes` their code column. The read is total: a row whose code is not a bare number fails `contract_table`, where it would have been read as no row. The source's codes are read from code alone, lib's pages apart, so a page's prose cannot hold a stale row green. `version_literal_sites` reads the top level's Markdown whole, the release notes apart, instead of naming the workroom's files, so the workroom's own contracts are still scanned for a version literal without a shipped file naming them, and it no longer hides grep's read errors.
- **The shipped comments that cited usage-rules.md** say what they meant without it: lib/builtins and buildfmt.bats name the README, which prettier would re-pad; lib/cmd/clean's says a false green is worse than a failure; shell-init's says the snippet was prose in a second document; neutral.bats's says review holds a name in prose.
- **workroom.bats's pointer arm** passes .gitignore alone, since .prettierignore no longer ships. README.md's and docs/migration.md's advice to fence the vendored runtime in a project's own .prettierignore is product advice, and stays; the release notes keep their history.

- **Done when 1.** tests/shipped.paths, at the bank's commit, lists none of the three, and lists VERSION, .gitignore, .gitattributes and design/.
- **Done when 2.** documentation.bats's two arms tagged (0241), "every exit code the source can return is named in the contract (0241)" and "the contract names no exit code the source cannot return (0241)", hold the table to the source's `exit N` statements both ways, and the first's failure prints the table. "the exit-code extractors read code and prose, and neither returns an empty set" fails on a row `contract_table` cannot read and on an empty set either side. usage-rules.md:58 points at the table.
- **Done when 3.** No shipped comment in lib/builtins, lib/cmd/clean, lib/cmd/shell-init, tests/unit/buildfmt.bats or tests/unit/neutral.bats names usage-rules.md, and .intent_critic.yml is named by no shipped file. Checked at the bank's commit and at its tip with `git grep -n -E 'usage-rules|intent_critic' <rev> -- <the specs of tests/shipped.paths> ':(exclude)CHANGELOG.md' ':(exclude)RELEASES/' ':(exclude)RELEASES.md'`, one line is left: bin/devbin:259's comment, "an explicit -h exits 0 (usage-rules.md)", which the issue's Measured list did not name. workroom.bats exempts no path that no longer ships.
- **Done when 4.** The landing suite: C's arms phase, in estate slot 01M61TNPWJTZMYNDBPTEZZ54ZG on molt-vc's grant, ran every arm tagged with one of the bank's eight issues on main 09c7d61a, file by file, from 2026-10-28 18:00Z to 18:08Z: in the red clone f4b30a50, main's lib with the bank's tests, under BSD; then at the bank's tip 53c92332 under BSD, and again with GNU coreutils, findutils, sed and grep first on PATH (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/s5e/runs/arms/, summary in s5e/arms.out). Of 0241's two arms, one failed in the red clone, and the other, that the contract names no exit code the source cannot return, passed there, as it should on main; both passed under BSD and GNU. C was stopped on hv's word in its light phase, so its whole-file legs, the tree scans among them, did not finish; hv's runs on main took them over. No later fix touched its code. hv's `dvb test all` on rhadamanth at 217adf65 ran every one of the 2777 tests bats counts in tests/unit once, and none failed (tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out, its .errors empty). K0116B, the full suite on kovacs at 4d1a76b0 with rustup's cargo first on PATH, as on CI's Ubuntu runner, is green, as vc read its seal. CI run 40851772728 on 4d1a76b0 and CI run 40860048152 on 25175386, the head 0.1.16 was cut from, are green on Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary. No critic leg ran on the landed commits.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
